sources.note: Nothing. Sociolinguistic loanword-domain study (78 Kanuri loans); the only phonology is a summary of Dlibugunaya 2016 on (Central) Margi consonant/vowel distribution. 'LANGUAGE: WEST MARGI (Margi Pute)', informant Abagana Kwalli Pshelkuba of Gumsuri; 'WEST MARGI Notes' (CONSONANTS 1-10, VOWELS 1-3) on pp. ~69-71, followed by the 434-item list.

sources.note: Google Books snippets only (no preview; not on archive.org). The two pages of notes cover consonants and vowels; stress appears once, incidentally, in VOWELS note: '[ə] appears to be a variant of /a/, usually in closed syllables (1,125). In open syllables it may be weakly stressed or unstressed and in fact in the closely related languages it usually corresponds to /a/'. No heading or rule for stress placement surfaced under any probe ('stress', 'penultimate', 'final syllable', 'TONE'); for another list (Chip) Kraft writes 'stress is not marked in the data'.
